Claude Code Hooks — Complete Reference

Every hook event Claude Code supports, when each fires, the stdin payload, exit-code semantics, and what it can do. Internal team reference for the UAL-ClaudeWorkflow template.

Version notes embedded throughout. Some events require Claude Code v2.1.70+. The /hooks command in Claude Code shows which events your installed version supports.

Overview — how hooks work

Claude Code supports 27+ lifecycle hook events that execute at specific points during a session. Each hook can be triggered by shell commands, HTTP endpoints, LLM prompts, MCP tools, or subagents. Hooks communicate via stdin (JSON input), stdout/stderr, and exit codes.

Configuration lives in settings.json / settings.local.json under the hooks object, keyed by event name:

{
  "hooks": {
    "PreToolUse": [
      {
        "matcher": "Bash",
        "hooks": [
          {
            "type": "command",
            "command": "node \"$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claude/hooks/my-bash-safety.cjs\""
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}

Every hook receives these base fields on stdin:

{
  "session_id": "abc123",
  "transcript_path": "/path/to/transcript.jsonl",
  "cwd": "/current/directory",
  "permission_mode": "default|plan|auto|dontAsk|bypassPermissions",
  "hook_event_name": "<event-name>"
}

Plus event-specific fields documented below.

Badges: blocks on exit 2 means this event can stop the action with exit code 2. non-blocking means exit codes other than 0 produce a debug log entry but the action proceeds. info-only means all exit codes and output are ignored — purely observational. used in template means this template's harness layer wires this event.

Lifecycle hooks

SessionStart non-blocking used in template

When it fires

Session begins or resumes.

Matcher syntax

"matcher": "startup|resume|clear|compact"
  • startup — initial session launch
  • resume — resuming a previous session
  • clear — after /clear command
  • compact — after context compaction

Stdin payload

{
  "session_id": "abc123",
  "transcript_path": "/path/to/transcript.jsonl",
  "cwd": "/current/directory",
  "permission_mode": "default",
  "hook_event_name": "SessionStart",
  "source": "startup|resume|clear|compact",
  "model": "claude-sonnet-4-6"
}

Stdout behavior

Text written to stdout is injected into Claude's context as a system reminder. Useful for injecting project conventions, current working context, or environment status.

Exit code semantics

  • 0: Session proceeds; stdout is injected as context
  • 2: stderr shown to user; session continues (cannot block SessionStart)
  • Other: Non-blocking error; stderr in debug log

Lifecycle position

First hook fired in any session, before Claude processes any prompts or sees any transcript history.

Common use cases

  1. Context re-injection after compaction — re-inject sprint goals, task notes, persona reminder
  2. Environment setup — load env vars, project state, dynamic context
  3. Conventions reminder — "Use Bun, not npm. Run bun test before committing."

Version notes

compact matcher added in v2.1.70. CLAUDE_ENV_FILE support requires v2.1.60+.

This template uses it

Two entries in .claude/settings.json:

  • matcher startup|resume|clear|compact → session-start-env-dump.cjs (project state JSON envelope)
  • matcher compact only → post-compact-restore.cjs (Unity rehydration with cache-friendly STABLE PREFIX + DYNAMIC SUFFIX; see .claude/WORKFLOW.md §POST-COMPACT REHYDRATION)

SessionEnd info-only

When it fires

Session terminates (exit, clear, logout, or context compaction that clears memory).

Matcher syntax

"matcher": "clear|resume|logout|prompt_input_exit|bypass_permissions_disabled|other"

Stdin payload

{
  "hook_event_name": "SessionEnd",
  "end_reason": "clear|resume|logout|prompt_input_exit|bypass_permissions_disabled|other"
  // ...plus base fields
}

Stdout / exit codes

Ignored. Event is informational only.

Lifecycle position

Final event in any session, after all cleanup but before process exit.

Common use cases

  1. Archive transcript for later review
  2. Cleanup — delete temp files, close DB connections, revoke short-term tokens
  3. Logging session duration / final state

UserPromptSubmit blocks on exit 2 used in template

When it fires

User submits a prompt, before Claude processes it.

Matcher syntax

No matcher support — fires on every prompt submission.

Stdin payload

{
  "hook_event_name": "UserPromptSubmit",
  "prompt": "The user's exact prompt text"
  // ...plus base fields
}

Stdout behavior

Exit 0 with JSON containing additionalContext field adds text to Claude's context. Text is injected as a system reminder before Claude reads the prompt.

Exit code semantics

  • 0: Prompt proceeds; stdout is injected as context
  • 2: stderr shown to user; prompt submission is blocked
  • Other: Non-blocking error; stderr in debug log

Common use cases

  1. Prompt validation/filtering — block certain commands or patterns
  2. Context augmentation — inject branch / time / project metadata before processing
  3. Audit logging

This template uses it

user-prompt-state-refresh.cjs — injects compact between-turn recap (branch, opt-in state, TODO in_progress, YOLO state). When YOLO is active, also injects the three-tier cascade state table.

UserPromptExpansion blocks on exit 2 used in template

When it fires

A user-typed / command or skill expands into a prompt, before Claude sees it. This is the "skill hook" event.

Matcher syntax

Skill/command name — "matcher": "my-skill|other-command|*". Use * to match every skill.

Stdin payload

{
  "hook_event_name": "UserPromptExpansion",
  "command_name": "my-skill",
  "expanded_prompt": "Full expanded prompt text"
  // ...plus base fields
}

Stdout behavior

Exit 0 with JSON: updatedPrompt rewrites the expansion; additionalContext prepends extra context.

{
  "hookSpecificOutput": {
    "hookEventName": "UserPromptExpansion",
    "updatedPrompt": "Modified prompt text",
    "additionalContext": "Extra context for Claude"
  }
}

Exit code semantics

  • 0: Expansion proceeds; JSON output applied
  • 2: Expansion blocked; stderr shown to user
  • Other: Non-blocking error; expansion proceeds

Common use cases

  1. Block certain commands — prevent dangerous skills
  2. Audit logging — record which commands are used
  3. Modify command behavior — rewrite skill parameters before execution
  4. Inject session-state context (this template's pattern)

Version notes

Introduced in v2.1.72. Older Claude Code versions silently ignore hooks wired to this event.

This template uses it

skill-context-inject.cjs with matcher * — injects YOLO three-tier cascade state when YOLO is active, plus per-skill reminders for /unity / /girlfriend / /housewife / /kittycat / /wild / /strict / /feral / /sweet / /cozy / /purr / /workflow / /yolo / /sober. See .claude/WORKFLOW.md §SKILL HOOKS.

Stop non-blocking via exit; blocks via JSON used in template

When it fires

Claude finishes responding (end of a turn).

Matcher syntax

No matcher support — fires on every turn completion.

Stdin payload

{
  "hook_event_name": "Stop",
  "stop_hook_active": false,
  "tool_calls_count": 5,
  "tokens_used": 12500
  // ...plus base fields
}

Stdout behavior

JSON output with decision: "block" tells Claude to keep working; reason field is fed to Claude as a new instruction. additionalContext is injected as next instruction.

{
  "decision": "block",
  "reason": "Not all tasks are complete. Still need to: 1) update tests, 2) merge main"
}

Exit code semantics

  • 0: Claude can stop; JSON output controls behavior
  • 2: stderr shown to user; Claude stops anyway (cannot block via exit 2)
  • Other: Non-blocking error; Claude stops
Infinite loop warning: If your Stop hook always returns block, Claude will loop indefinitely. Use stop_hook_active: true on stdin to detect recursive triggers and exit early.

Common use cases

  1. Verify task completion — ask an LLM hook if all requested work is done
  2. Quality gates — run tests and force fixes before Claude stops
  3. Progress tracking — verify checklist items completed

This template uses it

stop-session-writeup.cjs — writes .claude/.last-session.md with branch + TODO + last-FINALIZED summary. Read by next session's SessionStart.

StopFailure info-only

When it fires

Turn ends due to an API error (rate limit, authentication, server error, etc.).

Matcher syntax

"matcher": "rate_limit|authentication_failed|oauth_org_not_allowed|billing_error|invalid_request|server_error|max_output_tokens|unknown"

Stdin payload

{
  "hook_event_name": "StopFailure",
  "error_type": "rate_limit|authentication_failed|...",
  "error_message": "Rate limit exceeded: 100 requests per minute"
}

Stdout / exit codes

Ignored. Event is informational only.

Common use cases

  1. Logging API errors for diagnostics
  2. Notification when auth or billing errors occur
  3. Monitoring rate limit occurrences

Notification non-blocking

When it fires

Claude Code sends a notification — Claude is waiting for input or action.

Matcher syntax

"matcher": "permission_prompt|idle_prompt|auth_success|elicitation_dialog|elicitation_complete|elicitation_response"

Or empty string to match all types.

Stdin payload

{
  "hook_event_name": "Notification",
  "notification_type": "permission_prompt|idle_prompt|..."
}

Common use cases

  1. Desktop notifications — macOS osascript, Linux notify-send, Windows PowerShell pop-ups
  2. Slack/email alerts when Claude needs input
  3. Custom logging when Claude is idle or waiting

Example (macOS)

osascript -e 'display notification "Claude needs your attention" with title "Claude Code"'

Tool hooks

PreToolUse blocks on exit 2 or JSON deny used in template

When it fires

Before a tool executes (Bash, Edit, Write, Read, Glob, Grep, Agent, WebFetch, WebSearch, or MCP tools).

Matcher syntax

Tool name exact match or regex:

  • "matcher": "Bash" — Bash commands only
  • "matcher": "Edit|Write" — file editing only
  • "matcher": "mcp__.*" — all MCP tools
  • "matcher": "mcp__github__.*" — GitHub server tools only

Optional filter: "if": "Bash(rm *)" narrows handler to specific tool arguments.

Stdin payload

{
  "hook_event_name": "PreToolUse",
  "tool_name": "Bash",
  "tool_input": { "command": "npm test" },
  "tool_use_id": "toolu_01abc123def"
  // ...plus base fields
}

Stdout behavior

{
  "hookSpecificOutput": {
    "hookEventName": "PreToolUse",
    "permissionDecision": "allow|deny|ask|defer",
    "permissionDecisionReason": "Optional explanation to Claude",
    "updatedInput": { "command": "modified command" },
    "additionalContext": "Extra context for Claude"
  }
}

Exit code semantics

  • 0: Tool proceeds; JSON output controls behavior:
    • "allow" — skip user permission prompt (deny/ask rules still apply)
    • "deny" — block the tool; permissionDecisionReason sent to Claude
    • "ask" — show user permission dialog
    • "defer" — pause for external handling (requires -p headless mode; v2.1.82+)
  • 2: Tool is blocked; stderr shown to Claude as error feedback
  • Other: Non-blocking error; tool proceeds; stderr in debug log

Common use cases

  1. Block destructive commands — rm -rf, drop table, production deploys
  2. Enforce security policies — deny SSH to prod, block database writes
  3. Modify tool input — rewrite grep to rg, inject --dry-run flags
  4. Track tool use for audit compliance

Version notes

updatedInput field added in v2.1.80. defer decision added in v2.1.82 (headless-only). if field support added in v2.1.85.

This template uses it

pre-tool-bash-safety.cjs with matcher Bash — blocks three classes of dangerous commands: project-root deletion, system-path deletion, privileged commands (sudo / su / doas / runas / RunAs). The only blocking hook in the template's harness layer.

PostToolUse blocks via JSON used in template

When it fires

After a tool succeeds.

Matcher syntax

Same as PreToolUse — tool name exact match or regex.

Stdin payload

Identical to PreToolUse, plus tool_output (the tool's result):

{
  "hook_event_name": "PostToolUse",
  "tool_name": "Bash",
  "tool_input": { "command": "npm test" },
  "tool_use_id": "toolu_01abc123def",
  "tool_output": "PASS: 42 tests passed\n..."
}

Stdout behavior

{
  "decision": "block",
  "reason": "Reason for blocking further execution",
  "hookSpecificOutput": {
    "hookEventName": "PostToolUse",
    "additionalContext": "Text for Claude"
  }
}

Exit code semantics

  • 0: Tool execution succeeds; JSON output applied
  • 2: Execution blocked; Claude is told the action failed
  • Other: Non-blocking error; tool succeeds anyway
Important: Cannot undo actions already taken by the tool — the tool already ran. Use this hook to react to results, not prevent them.

Common use cases

  1. Auto-format code — run Prettier on every file edit
  2. Linting checks — validate code style and fail if violations found
  3. Logging file modifications
  4. Test automation after code changes

This template uses it

post-tool-memory-sync.cjs with matcher Edit|Write|MultiEdit — auto-syncs .claude/memory-templates/ edits to the Claude Code project memory folder under the user's home directory (~/.claude/projects/<encoded>/memory/).

PostToolUseFailure non-blocking

When it fires

After a tool fails or errors.

Matcher syntax

Tool name exact match or regex (same as PreToolUse / PostToolUse).

Stdin payload

{
  "hook_event_name": "PostToolUseFailure",
  "tool_name": "Bash",
  "tool_input": { "command": "npm test" },
  "tool_use_id": "toolu_01abc123def",
  "tool_error": "command not found: npm",
  "tool_error_type": "execution_error|timeout|invalid_input"
}

Exit code semantics

  • 0: Continue; JSON with additionalContext injected
  • Other: Non-blocking error; tool failure proceeds as normal
Exit code 2 does NOT block — the tool already failed. Returning 2 just shows stderr to user.

Common use cases

  1. Error recovery suggestions — detect common errors, suggest fixes
  2. Debugging context — inject diagnostic info (disk space, process list, logs)
  3. Notification on critical tool failures

Permission hooks

PermissionRequest non-blocking via exit; controls via JSON

When it fires

Claude Code is about to show a permission dialog (user approval needed for a tool).

Matcher syntax

"matcher": "Bash|Edit|ExitPlanMode|*"

Stdin payload

{
  "hook_event_name": "PermissionRequest",
  "tool_name": "Bash",
  "tool_input": { "command": "npm test" },
  "permission_mode": "default|plan|auto|dontAsk|bypassPermissions"
}

Stdout behavior

{
  "hookSpecificOutput": {
    "hookEventName": "PermissionRequest",
    "decision": {
      "behavior": "allow|deny|ask",
      "updatedPermissions": [
        {
          "type": "setMode",
          "mode": "acceptEdits|bypassPermissions",
          "destination": "session"
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}
Headless mode caveat: Does NOT fire in non-interactive (-p) mode. Use PreToolUse for headless permission logic.

Common use cases

  1. Auto-approve specific tools — skip prompt for low-risk commands
  2. Permission escalation — switch session to acceptEdits based on hook decision
  3. Audit logging

Version notes

Introduced in v2.1.75.

PermissionDenied non-blocking

When it fires

A tool call is denied by the auto-mode classifier (automated decision system).

Matcher syntax

Tool name (same as PermissionRequest).

Stdin payload

{
  "hook_event_name": "PermissionDenied",
  "tool_name": "Bash",
  "tool_input": { "command": "rm -rf /" },
  "denial_reason": "Dangerous command"
}

Stdout behavior

{
  "retry": true,
  "reason": "You can retry this command if you include --confirm flag"
}

Common use cases

  1. Allow retries — tell Claude it can retry with different arguments
  2. Context injection — suggest a safer alternative tool or approach
  3. Logging when auto-mode denies commands

Compaction hooks

PreCompact cannot prevent compaction used in template

When it fires

Before Claude's context compaction (when context window fills up).

Matcher syntax

"matcher": "manual|auto"
  • manual — user ran /compact command
  • auto — harness triggered compaction automatically

Stdin payload

{
  "hook_event_name": "PreCompact",
  "source": "manual|auto",
  "context_used": 85000,
  "context_limit": 100000
}

Stdout / exit codes

Ignored. Hooks cannot prevent compaction.

Common use cases

  1. Snapshot current state to disk before context is summarized
  2. Logging compaction occurrences
  3. Notification that context is about to be pruned

Version notes

Introduced in v2.1.70.

This template uses it

pre-compact-snapshot.cjs — writes .claude/.session-state.md with TODO state, git state, Git Flow context, files-just-touched, and curated session tidbits. Surfaced back into the post-compact context envelope by post-compact-restore.cjs.

PostCompact non-blocking

When it fires

After context compaction completes.

Matcher syntax

"matcher": "manual|auto"

Stdin payload

{
  "hook_event_name": "PostCompact",
  "source": "manual|auto",
  "context_recovered": 50000,
  "context_used_after": 35000
}

Stdout behavior

JSON with additionalContext is injected into Claude's context. Ideal place to re-inject critical project context lost in summarization.

{
  "additionalContext": "Critical project state to re-inject:\n- Current sprint: Q2 auth refactor\n- Last commit: abc123def"
}

Version notes

Introduced in v2.1.76.

Note: The template currently uses SessionStart with matcher: "compact" instead of literal PostCompact for back-compat with v2.1.70–v2.1.75. The two events overlap functionally.

Subagent & worktree hooks

SubagentStart non-blocking

When it fires

A subagent is spawned (via /agent, task delegation, or isolation: "subagent").

Matcher syntax

"matcher": "general-purpose|Explore|Plan|TaskDecomposition"

Or custom agent names.

Stdin payload

{
  "hook_event_name": "SubagentStart",
  "agent_type": "general-purpose|Explore|Plan|TaskDecomposition",
  "agent_name": "my-custom-agent",
  "parent_session_id": "parent-abc123"
}

Common use cases

  1. Environment setup for the isolated subagent
  2. Context injection — load parent session state
  3. Logging subagent creation

SubagentStop info-only

When it fires

A subagent finishes (task complete, error, or timeout).

Stdin payload

{
  "hook_event_name": "SubagentStop",
  "agent_type": "general-purpose|Explore|Plan|TaskDecomposition",
  "stop_reason": "completed|error|timeout|interrupted"
}

Common use cases

  1. Cleanup — release subagent-specific resources
  2. Logging
  3. Worktree cleanup if subagent used isolation: "worktree"

WorktreeCreate info-only

When it fires

A worktree is being created (via --worktree flag or isolation: "worktree").

Stdin payload

{
  "hook_event_name": "WorktreeCreate",
  "worktree_path": "/tmp/claude-worktree-xyz",
  "parent_branch": "main",
  "new_branch": "feature/new-feature"
}

WorktreeRemove info-only

When it fires

A worktree is being removed.

Stdin payload

{
  "hook_event_name": "WorktreeRemove",
  "worktree_path": "/tmp/claude-worktree-xyz",
  "removal_reason": "subagent_complete|session_exit|error"
}

TeammateIdle info-only

When it fires

An agent team teammate is about to go idle (Agent SDK only).

Stdin payload

{
  "hook_event_name": "TeammateIdle",
  "teammate_id": "teammate-123",
  "teammate_role": "architect|coder|reviewer"
}

MCP elicitation hooks

Elicitation info-only

When it fires

An MCP server requests user input during a tool call (opening an elicitation form/dialog).

Matcher syntax

"matcher": "my_server|github|slack"

Stdin payload

{
  "hook_event_name": "Elicitation",
  "mcp_server": "github",
  "tool_name": "mcp__github__create_pull_request",
  "elicitation_request": {
    "title": "PR Title",
    "description": "PR description"
  }
}

Version notes

Introduced in v2.1.75. Part of MCP elicitation flow.

ElicitationResult non-blocking; can rewrite response via JSON

When it fires

After a user responds to an MCP elicitation, before the response is sent back to the server.

Stdin payload

{
  "hook_event_name": "ElicitationResult",
  "mcp_server": "github",
  "tool_name": "mcp__github__create_pull_request",
  "elicitation_response": {
    "title": "User-entered PR Title",
    "description": "User-entered description"
  }
}

Stdout behavior

{
  "hookSpecificOutput": {
    "hookEventName": "ElicitationResult",
    "modifiedResponse": {
      "title": "Rewritten title"
    }
  }
}

Common use cases

  1. Validate user input before sending to server
  2. Sanitize input — remove sensitive data, enforce formatting
  3. Audit logging

Environment hooks

ConfigChange blocks via JSON

When it fires

A configuration file changes during a session (settings.json, skills, CLAUDE.md, or rules edited externally).

Matcher syntax

"matcher": "user_settings|project_settings|local_settings|policy_settings|skills"

Stdin payload

{
  "hook_event_name": "ConfigChange",
  "source": "user_settings|project_settings|local_settings|policy_settings|skills",
  "file_path": "/path/to/.claude/settings.json"
}

Stdout behavior — blocking

{
  "decision": "block",
  "reason": "Settings change not allowed in production"
}

Common use cases

  1. Audit logging — record who changed what for compliance
  2. Policy enforcement — block unauthorized changes to security settings
  3. Reload environment when project settings change

CwdChanged non-blocking; writes to CLAUDE_ENV_FILE

When it fires

Working directory changes (Claude runs cd command).

Stdin payload

{
  "hook_event_name": "CwdChanged",
  "old_cwd": "/previous/directory",
  "new_cwd": "/new/directory"
}

Special output — CLAUDE_ENV_FILE

Write shell script to $CLAUDE_ENV_FILE (path provided as env var). This file is sourced before every Bash command, so it can set environment variables dynamically per directory.

#!/bin/bash
direnv export bash > "$CLAUDE_ENV_FILE"

Common use cases

  1. Dynamic environment — reload env vars when directory changes (integrates with direnv, devbox, nix)
  2. Project-specific config — load .env per-directory
  3. Path setup — update PATH, Python venv, Node version when changing projects

FileChanged non-blocking; writes to CLAUDE_ENV_FILE

When it fires

A watched file changes on disk (modified externally, not by Claude).

Matcher syntax

"matcher": ".env|.envrc|package.json"
Matcher uses literal filenames (split on |), NOT regex. Different from most other events.

Stdin payload

{
  "hook_event_name": "FileChanged",
  "file_path": "/path/to/.env",
  "change_type": "modified|created|deleted"
}

Common use cases

  1. Environment reload when .env or .envrc changes
  2. Dependency setup when package.json / pyproject.toml changes
  3. Configuration sync

InstructionsLoaded info-only

When it fires

CLAUDE.md or .claude/rules/*.md files are loaded into Claude's context.

Matcher syntax

"matcher": "session_start|nested_traversal|path_glob_match|include|compact"

Stdin payload

{
  "hook_event_name": "InstructionsLoaded",
  "load_reason": "session_start|nested_traversal|...",
  "file_path": "/path/to/CLAUDE.md",
  "file_size": 5120
}

Task hooks (Agent SDK)

TaskCreated blocks on exit 2

When it fires

A task is being created (via TaskCreate in Agent SDK or subagent context).

Stdin payload

{
  "hook_event_name": "TaskCreated",
  "task_id": "task-abc123",
  "task_name": "Implement auth refactor",
  "task_description": "Full task description"
}

Exit code semantics

  • 0: Task is created as normal
  • 2: Task creation blocked; stderr shown; task is not created

Version notes

Requires Agent SDK or task system enabled.

TaskCompleted info-only

When it fires

A task is marked as completed.

Stdin payload

{
  "hook_event_name": "TaskCompleted",
  "task_id": "task-abc123",
  "task_name": "Implement auth refactor",
  "completion_status": "success|failed|abandoned"
}

Additional notes

Configuration locations & precedence

Hooks can be configured in multiple locations. More specific scopes override broader ones:

  1. Project-local (highest priority): .claude/settings.local.json (gitignored, personal)
  2. Project-shared: .claude/settings.json (committed to repo, team-wide)
  3. Plugin hooks: hooks/hooks.json in plugin package
  4. Skill/agent frontmatter: defined inline in .claude/commands/, .claude/skills/, or .claude/agents/
  5. User-global (lowest priority): ~/.claude/settings.json (across all projects)
  6. Managed policy (enforced): Managed settings from enterprise admin (cannot be disabled by user)

Parallel vs serial execution

  • Multiple hooks matching the same event execute in parallel by default
  • Identical hook commands are deduplicated (if two hooks run the same command, it runs once)
  • Exit codes from parallel hooks are combined: any hook exit-2 blocks; any ask prompts user
  • Hook execution order is non-deterministic when hooks run in parallel

Environment variables in hooks

$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIRAbsolute path to project root (always available)
$CLAUDE_ENV_FILEPath to script file for dynamic env vars (only in SessionStart, Setup, CwdChanged, FileChanged)
${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}Plugin installation directory (for plugin hooks)
${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}Plugin persistent data directory
$CLAUDE_EFFORTCurrent effort level (low, medium, high, xhigh, max) in Bash hooks

For HTTP headers, only variables listed in allowedEnvVars are interpolated.

Timeout behavior

  • Default timeout: 10 minutes (600 seconds)
  • Per-hook timeout: set "timeout": 30 (in seconds)
  • Command hooks: 600s default
  • Prompt hooks: 30s default
  • Agent hooks: 60s default
  • HTTP hooks: 30s default
  • When timeout expires: hook is killed; execution continues (non-blocking error)

Hook types reference

TypeExecutionInputOutputBest for
commandShell subprocessstdin JSONstdout/stderr + exit codeShell scripts, local commands
httpHTTP POSTJSON bodyJSON responseRemote services, team-wide hooks
mcp_toolMCP server tool callJSON inputJSON outputIntegrations with MCP servers
promptSingle LLM callJSON context{"ok": true|false}Yes/no decisions (fast)
agentSubagent spawnedJSON context{"ok": true|false, "reason": "..."}Complex verification (tool-capable)

Debugging hooks

  • Transcript view (Ctrl+O): one-line summary per hook (success silent; errors show first line of stderr)
  • Debug log (/debug mid-session): full hook execution details including exit codes, stdout, stderr
  • Manual testing: echo '{"tool_name":"Bash"}' | ./my-hook.sh && echo "Exit: $?"
  • The /hooks command: read-only browser of all configured hooks grouped by event

Common errors

  • hook error: jq: command not found — install jq or use Python/Node for JSON
  • hook error: command not found — use absolute paths or $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR
  • hook error: Permission denied — chmod +x ./hook.sh
  • JSON parse error — check shell profile for unconditional echo statements (wrap in if [[ $- == *i* ]]; then)

Disabling hooks

Global disable in any settings file:

{ "disableAllHooks": true }

Or delete individual hook entries from the hooks object.
